subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: Placing accents on weak or off beats
questions.explain: Syncopation stresses normally weak beats or off-beats, disrupting the regular pulse.

questions.q: Why is tuning important before an ensemble performs?
options: So all players sound in pitch with each other
questions.explain: Tuning ensures all players' pitches match so the ensemble sounds in tune together.

questions.q: 'Imitation' as a way of developing an idea means:
options: One part copies a melodic idea just stated by another part
questions.explain: Imitation is when one part copies a melodic idea introduced by another part.

questions.q: What does MIDI stand for in music technology?
questions.explain: MIDI stands for Musical Instrument Digital Interface, a protocol linking electronic instruments and computers.

questions.q: Which structure follows the pattern ABA?
questions.explain: Ternary form has three sections in an ABA pattern, where the A material returns.

questions.q: When sequencing in a DAW, individual notes are often arranged on a:
questions.explain: In a DAW, notes are commonly entered and arranged on a piano roll along a track timeline.

questions.q: The articulation marking 'staccato' tells a player to make notes:
questions.explain: Staccato means short and detached, the opposite of legato.

questions.q: A DAW used for recording and sequencing music stands for:
questions.explain: DAW means Digital Audio Workstation, software used to record, edit and sequence music.

questions.q: A rondo form is best described by which pattern?
questions.explain: In rondo form a main theme (A) returns between contrasting episodes, e.g. ABACA.

questions.q: In music, what does the dynamic marking 'forte' (f) mean?
questions.explain: Forte is an Italian dynamic term meaning loud, while piano means quiet.

questions.q: What does a 'crescendo' instruct a performer to do?
questions.explain: A crescendo is a gradual increase in volume, opposite to a diminuendo.

options: Playing music you have not seen before, at first sight
questions.explain: Sight-reading is performing a piece of music you are seeing for the first time.
